reasoning: Recent data for Minnesota’s 2026 U.S. Senate race indicate a Democratic-leaning environment, with structural ratings and available polling/forecasting all pointing to a modest but real Democratic edge statewide.[5][14] Cook Political Report’s characterization of the open Senate seat as “likely Democrat” with roughly a 3‑point advantage, combined with a forecasted general-election margin of about D+7 and a polling average around D+3.5, suggests the current general-election environment is best described as roughly D+3–D+5.[5][14] Within the last 45 days, most public numbers are primary-focused, but the aggregated forecast using polling up to mid-July remains the clearest quantitative guide to the present margin.[5]

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax’s Minnesota Senate forecast, based on three general-election polls through late May and updated with data through July 12, shows Democrats leading with a projected vote share of 53.6% to 46.5% (D+7.1), and a polling average of D 48.0% vs. R 44.5% (D+3.5).
sources.date_range: May 28, 2026 (polling through July 12, 2026; forecast last updated July 12, 2026)

sources.name: KSTP/SurveyUSA
sources.details: KSTP/SurveyUSA’s Minnesota polling shows the DFL-backed Peggy Flanagan and Rep. Angie Craig tied at 40%-40% in the Democratic Senate primary, while Michele Tafoya leads the GOP primary with 41%, highlighting competitive primaries but not providing general-election head-to-head numbers.

sources.name: Public Policy Polling via Native News Online
sources.details: A Public Policy Polling survey of 672 likely Democratic primary voters finds Peggy Flanagan leading Angie Craig 46% to 32% (D+14 within the primary electorate), showing Flanagan expanding her advantage in the DFL Senate primary but not measuring the general election.

sources.name: Mason-Dixon via News From The States
sources.details: A Mason-Dixon poll for a consortium of news organizations reports a generic Democrat leading a generic Republican for the Minnesota U.S. Senate seat 49% to 41% (D+8), and indicates that both leading Democrats (Craig and Flanagan) hold roughly 7‑point leads over GOP frontrunner Michele Tafoya in named matchups.
sources.date_range: Consortium poll "most recent 2026" (described in article; within 2026 cycle, no exact dates given)

sources.name: Cook Political Report via Los Angeles Blade
sources.details: Reporting on the Minnesota open Senate seat notes that The Cook Political Report rates the race as "likely Democrat" and describes roughly a 3‑point advantage for Democrats in the contest to succeed retiring Sen. Tina Smith.

sources.name: The Center Square summarizing SurveyUSA
sources.details: Coverage in The Center Square summarizing the same KSTP/SurveyUSA poll reports Flanagan and Craig tied at 40% in the DFL Senate primary and Tafoya leading the Republican primary with 41%, reinforcing a picture of competitive primaries without general-election margins.

sources.name: KSTP/SurveyUSA via Argo Journal
sources.details: A KSTP/SurveyUSA Minnesota Senate primary poll recap shows DFL primary tied 40%-40% between Craig and Flanagan and a strong Tafoya lead in the GOP primary, confirming intraparty dynamics but not offering the statewide November margin.
